key_insight: Training GPT-style models on synthetic limit order book data reveals they learn amortized Bayesian inference over hidden market regimes, not just next-token statistics.
engineering_relevance: This suggests foundation models for market microstructure can be used as fast, low-cost surrogates for regime estimation and simulator parameter calibration in trading-system design.
method: Train autoregressive transformers on synthetic order-flow streams from simulators with known latent states.
Compare model predictions against exact Bayes-optimal and oracle predictors using the known data entropy.
Probe frozen activations to decode latent regimes and test transfer to real NASDAQ order flow.
evidence_signal: Across controlled synthetic benchmarks, predictive loss matched the Bayes optimum to within a millinat per token and latent regimes were linearly decodable; on NASDAQ data, a richer simulator mixture nearly closed the zero-shot gap to an in-domain baseline.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on how well the simulator family covers real market dynamics, so poor prior coverage can limit zero-shot transfer despite strong synthetic performance.
paper_title: What Do Foundation Models for Market Microstructure Learn? A Controlled Study with Synthetic Limit Order Books
